title: A full Frobenius flag in the constructible Weil heart at a point
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, as in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $\mathcal F$ be any constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ in the raw/common-stage heart of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $(V,F)$ be its finite-dimensional geometric fibre with invertible local geometric Frobenius, using [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace; lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], and put $d=\dim_{\Qlb}V$. There is a full filtration by constructible Weil subsheaves
$$0=\mathcal F_0\subset\mathcal F_1\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal F_d=\mathcal F$$
whose fibre at stage $j$ has dimension $j$. Each quotient has one-dimensional fibre with Frobenius scalar $\alpha_j\in\Qlb^\times$, and is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $2\log_q|\iota(\alpha_j)|$. Its geometric fibre filtration is an $F$-invariant full flag, and $F$ restricts to an automorphism on every flag space and quotient. All these spaces, maps and Weil isomorphisms can be represented simultaneously at a single finite coefficient extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the raw coefficient heart, with the specified fibre and point-transport identifications. In particular $\mathcal F$ is mixed. The conclusion includes nontrivial Jordan blocks, requires no reality or semisimplicity hypothesis, and for $V=0$ gives the empty filtration. It holds with $k_0$ replaced by any finite extension, using that field's cardinality as $q$.

source.place: Paragraph 7: the dimension-zero Jordan filtration, invertible subquotient Frobenius and simultaneous finite coefficient-stage descent; returned Step 11.

proof.text: First choose an actual finite heart stage for the given sheaf. Write its underlying common-stage object as $(E_0,K)$. The constructible truncation theorem identifies $\mathcal H^0(E_0,K)$ with $(E_0,\mathcal H^0K)$, and the canonical truncation isomorphism identifies this with $\mathcal F$, since $\mathcal F$ is in the heart. Use this identification to replace the representative by the heart object $\mathcal H^0K$. Represent the Weil map, its inverse, the identification with the original object and its inverse at common finite stages. There are finitely many inverse and intertwining equations. By the equality rule in the Hom colimits, each holds at a further finite stage; a common upper bound makes all hold simultaneously. Thus, after one enlargement, there is a genuine heart object $M$ over $E_0$ with an isomorphism $\theta:Lg_s^*M\to M$ whose image is the prescribed Weil sheaf. No continuity of the powers of $\theta$ is required by the Weil-pair definition.

source.place: Paragraph 7, dimension-zero Jordan filtration; explicit point-heart and finite-stage argument by Q111.

proof.text: Use the stated point-fibre equivalence at finite coefficient fields together with the point-realization cohomology theorem. Its restriction to hearts is a fully faithful equivalence with finite-dimensional vector spaces: a heart object has fibre concentrated in degree zero; conversely, if a preimage $C$ of $W[0]$ is chosen under the equivalence, then $\mathcal H^0 C$ is a heart preimage, because $\operatorname{Fib}_s(\mathcal H^0 C)\cong H^0(\operatorname{Fib}_s C)[0]=W[0]$. Full faithfulness is inherited from the full derived subcategories. This equivalence preserves and reflects kernels and cokernels: their universal factorization properties transfer bijectively across the Hom bijections. It therefore preserves and reflects short exact sequences. These fibre identifications commute with enlarging the finite coefficient field by the scalar/cohomology compatibility in the point-realization theorem. In particular the fibre $V_0$ of $M$ is finite dimensional and $V=V_0\otimes_{E_0}\Qlb$.

source.place: Paragraph 7, dimension-zero Jordan filtration; explicit point-heart and finite-stage argument by Q111.

proof.text: Apply the invariant-flag theorem over the algebraically closed coefficient field $\Qlb$, rather than over the geometric base field $k$, to $F:V\to V$. It gives $0=W_0\subset W_1\subset\cdots\subset W_d=V$ with $\dim W_j=j$ and $F(W_j)\subset W_j$. Each restriction is injective because $F$ is, and sends a basis of $W_j$ to $j$ independent vectors in the $j$-dimensional space $W_j$; these form a basis. Hence $F(W_j)=W_j$ and also $F^{-1}(W_j)=W_j$. Thus $F$ and $F^{-1}$ induce mutually inverse operators on every $W_j/W_{j-1}$. Choose $b_j\in W_j\setminus W_{j-1}$ successively. Their images generate the one-dimensional successive quotients, so $b_1,\ldots,b_j$ is a basis of $W_j$. On the $j$th quotient the induced operator is multiplication by a scalar $\alpha_j$, nonzero because it is invertible. This argument allows repeated eigenvalues and nonzero off-diagonal entries.

source.place: Paragraph 7, dimension-zero Jordan filtration; explicit point-heart and finite-stage argument by Q111.

proof.text: Choose an $E_0$-basis of $V_0$. Let $B$ be the change-of-basis matrix whose columns are the adapted vectors $b_j$ in this basis after extension to $\Qlb$. Enlarge $E_0$ to a finite field $E\subset\Qlb$ containing all entries of $B$, $B^{-1}$ and the matrices of $F$ and $F^{-1}$ in the adapted basis. Such an extension is finite: every one of these finitely many entries is algebraic over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and adjoining them successively multiplies finitely many finite degrees. Put $W_{j,E}=\operatorname{span}_E(b_1,\ldots,b_j)$ inside $V_0\otimes_{E_0}E$. The triangular matrix equations for $F$ and $F^{-1}$ hold over $E$ because they hold in its containing field $\Qlb$. They preserve every $W_{j,E}$; the scalar on $W_{j,E}/W_{j-1,E}$ is $\alpha_j\in E^\times$. The coordinate inclusion and quotient maps, and the bases exhibiting their exact sequences, are now all over this same $E$.

source.place: Paragraph 7, dimension-zero Jordan filtration; explicit point-heart and finite-stage argument by Q111.

proof.text: At this finite stage use the heart equivalence in step 2 to choose heart objects $M_j$ with specified fibres $W_{j,E}$, taking $M_d=M\otimes_{E_0}E$. Write $A_j=F|_{W_{j,E}}$ under these identifications. Let $\iota_{M_j}:\operatorname{Fib}_s(M_j)\to\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*M_j)$ be the specified point transport. It is an isomorphism. Full faithfulness of the point-fibre equivalence lifts the map $A_j\circ\iota_{M_j}^{-1}$ uniquely to a map $\theta_j:Lg_s^*M_j\to M_j$; it lifts its inverse as well, so faithfulness gives the two inverse identities. Pullback along the scheme automorphism $g_s$ commutes with constructible truncations, hence both source and target are in the heart. Thus $(M_j,\theta_j)$ is an actual constructible $E$-Weil sheaf. For $j=d$, the equation $F=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\theta)\circ\iota_M$ in the definition of local Frobenius shows that this is exactly the original Weil structure after scalar extension, not a separately chosen automorphism.

source.place: Paragraph 7, dimension-zero Jordan filtration; explicit point-heart and finite-stage argument by Q111.

proof.text: Lift each vector inclusion $u:W_{j-1,E}\to W_{j,E}$ by full faithfulness. It is a monomorphism and its cokernel has the prescribed quotient fibre by the exact heart equivalence of step 2. Naturality of point transport says $\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*u)\iota_{M_{j-1}}=\iota_{M_j}\operatorname{Fib}_s(u)$. Combining this with $A_ju=uA_{j-1}$ and the formula in step 5 gives $\operatorname{Fib}_s(u\theta_{j-1})=\operatorname{Fib}_s(\theta_j Lg_s^*u)$; faithfulness proves Weil equivariance. For the cokernel $Q_j$, define its Weil isomorphism by lifting the induced quotient automorphism composed with $\iota_{Q_j}^{-1}$, just as in step 5. The same equation with the quotient projection makes that projection Weil equivariant. Therefore the lifted sequence is short exact in the underlying constructible heart, with the required Weil structures. Composition of the lifted inclusions makes $M_j$ a Weil subobject of $M_d$; pass to $\Qlb$ and identify the endpoint with $\mathcal F$. All these constructions and inverse maps were made at the single field $E$. After extension to $\Qlb$ the adapted coordinate bases still exhibit exact vector-space sequences; the same point equivalence and cohomology comparison at the common stage reflect their exactness in the common-stage heart.

source.place: Paragraph 7, dimension-zero Jordan filtration; explicit point-heart and finite-stage argument by Q111.

proof.text: The unique closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ has residue cardinality $q$. The specified fibre and point-transport identifications give local Frobenius $\alpha_j$ on the quotient, by the defining composite of local Frobenius and step 5. Since $\iota$ is a field isomorphism and $\alpha_j\ne0$, the number $r_j=|\iota(\alpha_j)|$ is positive. Put $w_j=2\log(r_j)/\log(q)$. Since $q>1$, $\log(q)>0$, and the positive real power convention gives $q^{w_j/2}=\exp((\log(r_j)/\log(q))\log(q))=r_j$. The purity definition therefore makes the quotient punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w_j$. The finite Weil filtration constructed above is exactly the mixedness filtration of that definition (and, when a bound is wanted, take the maximum of its finitely many weights).

source.place: Paragraph 7, dimension-zero Jordan filtration; explicit point-heart and finite-stage argument by Q111.

proof.text: If $d=0$, the faithful heart equivalence identifies $\mathcal F$ with zero; take the empty filtration with its sole endpoint $0=\mathcal F$. There are no quotient or weight conditions to check. For a finite extension of $k_0$, carry out the same construction with that finite field as the base datum and its cardinality $q'$ in the logarithmic calculation. The point equivalence, the natural invertible point transports, and the truncation assertions are stated for every finite-field datum, so the proof has the same hypotheses. No step imposed reality, diagonalizability, or semisimplicity.
